rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: HSE defines work-related violence as an incident in which a person is abused, threatened or assaulted in circumstances relating to work.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: Work-related violence can include verbal or online abuse, telephone threats and physical attacks.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: Health and safety law requires employers to protect workers from work-related violence so far as reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: Employers must assess significant violence risks, consult workers and implement effective control measures.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: A risk assessment by itself does not reduce violence; the actions taken after assessment are what reduce occurrence.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: Work-related violence can cause injury, stress, mental-health conditions, disability or death.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: Workers should use training, report violence or aggression and cooperate with prevention arrangements so employers can support them and improve controls.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: Lone workers, new starters, trainees and other vulnerable workers can face increased violence risk because support or experience may be limited.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: Violence risk depends on work activity, contact with the public, lone working, time, location, authority, valuables, prior incidents, staffing and control effectiveness.

rows.source: HSE work-related violence and aggression guidance
rows.verified: General definition, legal duties, assessment, controls, reporting, learning and worker support guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: The Display Screen Equipment Regulations apply to workers who use display screens daily for continuous periods of an hour or more.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers must carry out a display-screen workstation assessment for covered users.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: Employers must reduce display-screen risks, including arranging breaks or changes of activity.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: An eye test must be provided if a covered display-screen user asks for one.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: Display-screen users must receive health and safety training and information on risks and safe working practices.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: Poorly designed or incorrectly used display-screen work can contribute to musculoskeletal pain, fatigue and eye strain.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: Training should cover posture, furniture adjustment, desk layout, screen and lighting arrangement, breaks, assessments and problem reporting.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: A standard workstation setup places the top of the screen around eye level and the screen roughly an arm's length away.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: Display-screen risk depends on duration, workstation geometry, posture, input devices, vision needs, lighting, breaks, mobility and individual health factors.

rows.source: HSE display-screen-equipment safety guidance
rows.verified: General user scope, workstation assessment, breaks, eye tests, posture and training guidance does not prove the current condition, exposure or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact event or illness probability.
